story.title: Brazil Elections 2026
story.description: Live coverage of the first round of Brazil's general election, from the opening of the polls to the final count. Demo content: the events and figures are fictional.

images.title: A ballot box with three folded ballots
Voters queue outside a polling station

updates.title: Good morning from Brasília
updates.body: Welcome to our live coverage of election day. Polls open at 8:00 across the country, and more than 150 million voters are expected to choose a president, governors, senators and representatives.

updates.title: Polls are open
updates.body: Voting has started in every state. Polling stations stay open until 17:00, Brasília time.

updates.title: Long lines in São Paulo
updates.body: Our reporter in São Paulo describes queues around the block at several schools in the east of the city. Election officials say the lines are moving quickly.

updates.title: Electoral court reports a smooth start
updates.body: The electoral court says fewer than 0.1% of voting machines needed to be replaced in the first half hour, in line with previous elections.

updates.title: How the voting machine works
updates.body: Brazilians vote on electronic machines. Each voter types a number for each office, checks the candidate's photo on screen and presses the green CONFIRMA key.

updates.title: First candidates cast their votes
updates.body: Both front-runners voted early this morning, each surrounded by supporters and cameras. Neither took questions from the press.

updates.title: Rain in the South
updates.body: Heavy rain in Porto Alegre and Curitiba has not kept voters at home so far, officials say.

updates.title: What is at stake
updates.body: Besides the presidency, voters elect 27 governors, a third of the Senate and all 513 seats of the Chamber of Deputies.

updates.title: Turnout at 18% by 10:00
updates.body: The electoral court's first turnout figure is slightly ahead of the same hour in the last general election.

updates.title: Voting abroad
updates.body: Brazilians living in more than 100 countries are voting at embassies and consulates. Lisbon reports its longest queue ever.

updates.title: Machine replaced in Manaus
updates.body: A faulty voting machine was swapped at a school in Manaus. Votes already cast were recovered from its memory card, the regional court says.

updates.title: Fact check: no, you cannot vote by text message
updates.body: A message circulating on social networks claims voters can vote by sending an SMS. That is false: votes are only cast in person, on the machines.

updates.title: Indigenous communities vote by boat
updates.body: In the Amazon, election officials travelled for days by boat to bring voting machines to remote villages.

updates.title: Turnout at 31% by 11:00
updates.body: Turnout keeps pace with the morning's trend. The Northeast leads with 34%.

updates.title: Live from our newsroom
updates.body: Our editors are tracking results from every state. The first official numbers are expected shortly after polls close.

updates.title: Lunch-time lull
updates.body: Lines have shortened in most capitals as voters stop for lunch. Officials expect another peak in the afternoon.

updates.title: Arrests for vote buying
updates.body: Federal police report a handful of arrests for alleged vote buying in three states. No incident has disrupted voting.

updates.title: Turnout at 44% by noon
updates.body: Turnout is now two points ahead of the last general election at the same hour.

updates.title: Young voters
updates.body: More than two million 16- and 17-year-olds registered to vote, for whom voting is optional. Many are casting their first ballot today.

updates.title: Recap of the final debate
updates.body: The last televised debate, on Thursday, focused on the economy, public security and the environment. Polls taken afterwards showed little movement.

updates.title: Queues return in Rio
updates.body: Lines are building again in the North Zone of Rio de Janeiro, where several schools combine many polling sections.

updates.title: Turnout at 57% by 14:00
updates.body: The electoral court says the afternoon pace is steady. Final turnout in the last general election was 79%.

updates.title: Observers praise the process
updates.body: International observers say the vote has been calm and well organised so far, in a short statement from their mission in Brasília.

updates.title: Power cut in a polling station
updates.body: A brief power cut in Belém did not stop voting: the machines run on batteries for up to ten hours.

updates.title: Turnout at 66% by 15:00
updates.body: Two hours before the polls close, two in three registered voters have voted.

updates.title: Markets watch closely
updates.body: Analysts expect currency markets to react on Monday morning to the first-round results, especially if a second round is needed.

updates.title: Late voters rush in
updates.body: In Salvador and Recife, voters are arriving in numbers before the 17:00 deadline. Anyone in line at closing time may still vote.

updates.title: Turnout at 74% by 16:00
updates.body: Turnout is on course to match or exceed the last general election.

updates.title: How counting works
updates.body: When polls close, each machine prints a tally and sends its encrypted results to the electoral court. National totals usually arrive within hours.

updates.title: Polls close
updates.body: Voting has ended in every state except where voters are still in line. Counting begins now.

updates.title: First results
updates.body: With 5% of sections counted, the race is too close to call. Both leading candidates are within two points of each other.

updates.title: Results at 20%
updates.body: The first count shows a regional split familiar from previous elections, with the Northeast and the South leaning in opposite directions.

updates.title: Final turnout: 79%
updates.body: The electoral court confirms turnout of 79.4%, slightly above the last general election.

updates.title: Results at 45%
updates.body: Neither leading candidate is close to the 50% plus one needed to win outright. A second round looks increasingly likely.

updates.title: Governors elected in the first round
updates.body: At least nine states have elected their governors outright, according to the electoral court's projections.

updates.title: Results at 70%
updates.body: The gap between the two leading candidates has narrowed to under one point.

updates.title: Senate takes shape
updates.body: With most states counted, the new Senate will be more fragmented than the outgoing one, analysts say.

updates.title: Results at 90%
updates.body: The electoral court says the remaining sections are mostly from large cities, where counting takes longer.

updates.title: Second round confirmed
updates.body: With 98% of sections counted, no candidate can reach a majority. The two leading candidates will face each other in the second round on October 25.

updates.title: Celebrations in the capitals
updates.body: Supporters of both campaigns are celebrating in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Brasília, each claiming momentum for the second round.

updates.title: Candidates address supporters
updates.body: Both candidates thanked voters and called for calm. Campaigning for the second round begins tomorrow.

updates.title: Final result of the first round
updates.body: With 100% of sections counted, the electoral court has published the official first-round result. Turnout was 79.4%.

updates.title: That is all for tonight
updates.body: Thank you for following our live coverage. We will be back tomorrow morning with analysis and reactions from across the country.
